_about: Music of the Future: the host's own picks (sent 14 November 2026), in the order of the YouTube playlist. Chapter titles are the host's headings; notes marked host are the host's words, the rest come from each video's own credits. d = seconds on YouTube. embed: false = YouTube will not play it inside another page (age-restricted), so the page links out. The playlist on YouTube must keep this exact order.
title: Music of the Future

parts.title: The evening
parts.note: Short pieces, nearly all with their own videos: made for the projector.

parts.title: Long sets
parts.note: Two albums, a live-coded rave, a live session and a mix, then Arca to close. For later in the night.

chapters.title: Lift-off
chapters.note: The old dream of going out there: Carl Sagan's voice over the planets, mission control during Apollo 11, and Tokyo as a city of machines in 1979.

chapters.title: Holly Herndon — PROTO
chapters.note: Music co-written with AI, where you can't tell whether you are hearing the AI or real people.

chapters.title: AI as the main visual effect
Futuristic visuals
chapters.note: Three videos from Oneohtrix Point Never's Tranquilizer (2025), each by a different maker, then Björk.

chapters.title: Algo raves
chapters.note: Live coding: the music and the visuals are written as code in front of the crowd.

chapters.title: Arca — @@@@@
chapters.note: Music as the disintegration of identity, the body, gender and form. Very heavy, yet unexpected.

tracks.note: A short film: people among the moons and rings of the Solar System, with Carl Sagan reading from Pale Blue Dot.
